description:
Make `validate --json` use the canonical error envelope whenever validation ends with a nonzero process status, so validation obeys the same machine-readable failure contract as every other dispatched command.

## Background

The validation handler currently serializes its normal report shape with `valid: false` and then exits nonzero. That is useful result data, but it is not the canonical error-envelope shape required for failing machine-readable invocations. Successful validation remains a normal validation report; only failing outcomes move onto the shared error contract, with useful findings retained as structured detail.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: An integrity or rule failure from `validate --json` emits exactly one canonical error envelope on the payload stream instead of a raw `valid: false` report.
- [hard] REQ-02: The envelope reports a registered error code whose mapping determines the process exit status.
- [hard] REQ-03: The envelope retains the validation findings and integrity context needed by machine consumers as structured detail.
- [hard] REQ-04: A successful `validate --json` invocation still emits the normal successful validation report, and plain validation behavior remains unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-05: Integration coverage exercises successful JSON validation plus integrity-failure and rule-failure JSON validation, asserting payload shape, stream purity, and exit status.
title: Envelope failing validation reports
